test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which constitutional article ensures the protection of the cultural and educational rights of minorities?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 29**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 29** of the **Constitution of India** specifically deals with the **protection of interests of minorities**. It ensures that any section of the **citizens** residing in the territory of **India** having a distinct **language**, **script**, or **culture** of its own shall have the right to conserve the same. ***Hence, the option Article 29 is correct.***
 
• It serves two primary purposes: Clause (1) protects the right of a group to maintain its **cultural** and **linguistic** identity, while Clause (2) guarantees the individual right of a **citizen** not to be denied admission into **educational institutions** maintained by the **State** or receiving aid out of **State funds** on grounds only of **religion**, **race**, **caste**, **language**, or any of them.
 
• Though the heading of **Article 29** mentions "minorities," the use of the phrase "**section of citizens**" in the text indicates that the protection is available to both **minorities** as well as the **majority** community in certain contexts, as interpreted by the **Supreme Court of India**.
 
• This article is part of the **Cultural and Educational Rights** (Articles **29** and **30**) enshrined in **Part III** of the **Indian Constitution**, which are fundamental to the **secular** fabric of the **country**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 15**:
 
 
• This article prohibits **discrimination** by the **State** against any **citizen** on grounds only of **religion**, **race**, **caste**, **sex**, or **place of birth**.
 
• It is a facet of the **Right to Equality** (Articles **14** to **18**). It ensures equal access to **public places** like shops, restaurants, and wells. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect in the context of specific minority cultural rights.***
 
 
 
• **Article 25**:
 
 
• It provides for the **freedom of conscience** and the right to freely **profess**, **practice**, and **propagate** **religion** to all persons.
 
• This right is not absolute and is subject to **public order**, **morality**, and **health**. It also allows the **State** to regulate **economic**, **financial**, or **political** activities associated with **religious practice**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect as it deals with religious freedom rather than specific cultural/educational rights.***
 
 
 
• **Article 32**:
 
 
• Commonly referred to as the "**Right to Constitutional Remedies**," it allows **citizens** to move the **Supreme Court** for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights**.
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** famously described this article as the "**Heart and Soul of the Constitution**." It empowers the **court** to issue **writs** like **Habeas Corpus**, **Mandamus**, **Prohibition**, **Quo Warranto**, and **Certiorari**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect as it is a remedial right.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 30**: Complementary to **Article 29**, it grants all **minorities** (whether based on **religion** or **language**) the right to **establish** and **administer** **educational institutions** of their choice.
 
• The **Constitution of India** does not define the word "**minority**." However, **Article 30** recognizes minorities based on **religion** and **language**.
 
• In the **T.M.A. Pai Foundation case (2002)**, the **Supreme Court** ruled that for the purpose of **Article 30**, the unit for determining **minority status** is the **State**, not the whole of **India**.
 
• **Fundamental Rights** were borrowed from the **Constitution of the USA** (**Bill of Rights**) and are **justiciable** in nature, meaning they are enforceable by **courts**.
 
• The **National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992**, identifies six **religious minorities** in **India**: **Muslims**, **Christians**, **Sikhs**, **Buddhists**, **Zoroastrians (Parsis)**, and **Jains** (added in **2014**).
